slides.title: AI as a Smart Intern: The Power of Prompting
content: AI models are like smart, fast interns.
They need clear instructions to do good work.
Prompting is giving these instructions.
A good prompt leads to high-quality results.
narration: Imagine AI as a smart intern. It does amazing things but needs clear instructions. Prompting is giving these. A good prompt guides AI to get what you want. Let us understand the basics.
slides.image_prompt: An illustration of a friendly robot assistant or an 'intern' character with gears in its head, taking notes from a human. The human is holding a scroll with clear, detailed instructions written on it. Bright and engaging.

slides.title: The 3 C's: Clarity
content: Good prompts almost always include: Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
Clarity: Be specific! AI does not know what you are thinking.
Weak: "Write about electric cars."
Good: "Write a short blog post explaining the top 3 benefits of owning an electric car for city residents."
narration: Good prompts use the '3 C's': Clarity, Context, and Constraints.
First, Clarity: Be specific! AI does not know your thoughts.
'Write about electric cars' is a weak prompt.
A clear prompt gives details. For instance, explain the top 3 benefits of electric cars.
Specify 'for city residents' and 'short blog post'.
This approach avoids confusion.
slides.image_prompt: A split screen showing two prompts. On the left, a blurry, generic image represents a 'weak prompt' with vague text. On the right, a sharp, detailed image represents a 'clear prompt' with specific text, showing a lightbulb moment.

slides.title: The 3 C's: Context and Constraints + Persona
content: Context: Give background. Tell AI why and for whom.
Better Prompt (with Context): "Write for a sustainable lifestyle blog. Explain top 3 benefits of electric cars for city residents."
Constraints: Set rules. Define length, format, and style.
Excellent Prompt (with Constraints): "Write under 400 words, friendly tone, end with a question."
Bonus Tip: Provide a Persona. Tell AI who to be. Example: "Act as an expert travel agent."
narration: Second, Context: Give background.
Tell AI why and for whom.
For example, specify it is 'for a sustainable lifestyle blog'.
Also, add 'Explain top 3 benefits of electric cars for city residents'.
This makes your prompt much better.
Third, Constraints: Set rules like length, format, or style.
For example: 'Write under 400 words, friendly tone, end with a question'.
Also, give AI a Persona.
Say 'Act as an expert travel agent', for instance.
This makes your prompts more effective.
slides.image_prompt: A visual metaphor of building a layered cake. The base layer is 'Clarity', the second layer is 'Context' (a person's silhouette as audience), the top layer is 'Constraints' (a ruler or stopwatch). A chef's hat represents the 'Persona' on top of the cake.

slides.title: Giving Examples: Zero, One, and Few-Shot
content: Zero-Shot: You give zero examples. (Most common).
One-Shot: You give one example to show a pattern.
Example: "Summarize text like this: Text: 'Sun is a star.' Output: 'Primary celestial body: Sun'."
Few-Shot: You give a few examples for complex patterns.
narration: Sometimes examples help AI.
Zero-Shot: No examples, just ask.
One-Shot: One example for formatting.
For One-Shot, use one example. For instance:
Text: 'Sun is a star.' Output: 'Primary celestial body: Sun'.
Few-Shot involves a few examples for complex patterns.
These methods guide the AI's structure effectively.
slides.image_prompt: A visual representation of 'Zero, One, Few-Shot' concept. Three light bulbs: one is off (zero-shot), one is dimly lit with a single example text bubble (one-shot), and one is brightly lit with multiple example text bubbles (few-shot). Gears are turning in the background representing AI processing.

slides.title: Advanced Techniques: Chain-of-Thought (CoT)
content: Chain-of-Thought (CoT): Ask AI to "Think Step-by-Step".
Useful for logic, math, reasoning problems.
Reduces errors by showing AI's logic.
Prompt: "I have 5 boxes of apples, 12 in each. I eat 3, give away 1 full box. How many left? Think step-by-step."
narration: Advanced prompting: Chain-of-Thought (CoT). Ask AI to 'Think step-by-step.' This helps with logic and math. It forces AI to show its logic, reducing errors. Consider this example prompt: '5 boxes of 12 apples. Eat 3, give away 1 box. How many left? Think step-by-step.' This is powerful.
slides.image_prompt: A graphic showing a winding path or a series of interconnected thought bubbles leading to a final answer. Each bubble contains a small calculation or logical step. A magnifying glass hovers over the path, emphasizing detailed thinking.

slides.title: Advanced Techniques: Structuring Output & Iterative Prompting
content: Structuring Output: Tell AI the exact format you need (Markdown table, HTML, JSON, list).
Prompt: "List pros and cons of remote work as a Markdown table with 'Pros' and 'Cons' columns."
Iterative Prompting: It is a conversation! Refine prompts based on AI's replies.
narration: Next, Structuring Output. Tell AI how to present information. Ask for Markdown tables, HTML, or bullet points. This saves your time. Finally, Iterative Prompting: It is a conversation. Refine prompts based on AI's replies. Guide it until perfect. This back-and-forth gives great results.
slides.image_prompt: A split image. On one side, a blueprint or schema with different shapes (table, list, JSON icons) representing structured output. On the other side, two speech bubbles going back and forth, showing a refining conversation flow, with a 'thumbs up' icon at the end.

slides.title: Practical Lab: Text Generation Challenge
content: Open Google Gemini, ChatGPT, or Claude.

Try this prompt: "Act as a fitness coach. Create a simple 3-day workout plan for a beginner who wants to exercise at home with no equipment. The goal is a full-body workout. Present it in a table format with columns for 'Day', 'Exercise', and 'Duration'."
Pause the video and try this yourself!
narration: Time to practice! Open an AI tool.
Combine Persona, 3 C's, and structured output.
Let us try a prompt. Give AI a persona: 'Act as a fitness coach'.
Ask it to create a '3-day home workout plan for a beginner'.
Set the goal as 'full-body'.
Request the output in a table format.
Use columns for 'Day', 'Exercise', and 'Duration'.
Pause and try this yourself!
See the amazing power of detailed prompts!
slides.image_prompt: A split screen. On one side, a screenshot of a generic AI chat interface with the challenge prompt entered. On the other side, an illustration of a person doing a simple home workout, smiling. A 'Pause' icon is prominent.
slides.video_prompt: Screen recording of opening an LLM, typing the given prompt, hitting enter, and then showcasing the tabular output. The screen should be clean and readable. Highlight the table format.

slides.title: Practical Lab: Image Prompting Challenge
content: Image tools like Midjourney or DALL-E 3 use descriptive prompts.
Think like an artist: describe visual details.
Try this: "A close-up, photorealistic image of a cat wearing a tiny detective hat and magnifying glass, sitting in a library. The lighting is warm and cinematic."
Use Midjourney or DALL-E 3 if available.
narration: Prompting also works for image tools.
Describe visual details like an artist would.
Look at the prompt on the slide.
It asks for a 'close-up, photorealistic cat with a tiny detective hat'.
Also, a 'magnifying glass, in a library'.
And specify 'warm, cinematic lighting'.
Pause and experiment with this prompt.
Practice improves your results for both text and images.
slides.image_prompt: A split screen. On one side, a text input field for an image generation tool with the prompt entered. On the other side, a generated image matching the description: a photorealistic cat detective in a library. A 'Pause' icon is prominent.
slides.video_prompt: Screen recording of opening an image generation tool (e.g., Midjourney or DALL-E 3 web interface), typing the given image prompt, hitting enter, and showing the generated image result. Emphasize the detailed output.

slides.title: Summary
content: AI needs specific instructions (prompts).
Good prompts have Clarity, Context, Constraints (3 C's).
Use Persona and examples (Zero, One, Few-Shot).
Advanced techniques: Chain-of-Thought, structured output, iterative prompting.
Practice is key for effective prompting.
narration: Summary: AI needs clear prompts.
Use 3 C's: Clarity, Context, Constraints.
Add Persona and examples like Zero, One, or Few-Shot.
Advanced techniques include Chain-of-Thought and structured output.
Also use iterative prompting.
Keep practicing for amazing AI results!
Now, let us move to a small assignment.

slides.title: Assignment
content: Use an AI tool (Gemini/ChatGPT/Claude).

Prompt: "Act as a friendly tour guide for Mumbai. Create a 1-day itinerary for a family visiting Mumbai for the first time. They want to see historical places and try local street food. Include time estimates. Present this as a bulleted list with timings."
Observe the output and refine your prompt if needed.
narration: Your assignment: Use an AI tool. Your prompt is: 'Act as a friendly tour guide for Mumbai. Create a 1-day itinerary for a family, first-time visitors. Include historical places and street food, with time estimates. Present this as a bulleted list.' Apply 3 C's and refine your prompt. This will strengthen your skills.
